title: Verifier-Gated LLM NetOps: A Preregistered, Artifact-backed Evaluation of Input-Sanitization and Deterministic Verification Against Adversarial Intents
abstract: We report a preregistered confirmatory experiment (study_id cand-2026-03) that measured whether template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating (plus at-most-one automated repair) changes the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated CLI configurations under adversarially crafted intents. The preregistered primary estimand was the paired difference in per-intent validator acceptance-for-deployment (guarded − baseline). The frozen run used 150 adversarial intents (planned episodes = 300; completed episodes = 282; complete paired outcomes = 141) with a single generator (gpt-5-mini) and deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Observed outcomes: baseline accepted 135/141 (95.7447%); guarded accepted 141/141 (100.0%); paired difference = 0.04255319; exact two-sided McNemar p = 0.03125; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.01418440, 0.07801418]. Review-driven clarifications (preregistration wording vs formal estimand, per-condition pipeline timeline and evidence for shared_initial_candidate reuse, and an unset runtime temperature in the archived model configuration) are incorporated and reconciled with explicit artifact references. Major limitations (synthetic tasks, single model and validator, and an unexecuted benign-control) constrain external generalization. All numeric claims are supported by archived execution and analysis artifacts referenced in Methods and Results.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) can translate operator intent into device CLI, promising labor savings for network operations (NetOps) but introducing syntax, topology and semantic risks and new attack surfaces such as prompt injection. Prior prototype work shows that coupling LLM generation with deterministic verification and localized repair reduces some error classes and improves deployability of generated configurations [1]–[4]. However, operationally meaningful evaluation practices remain fragmented: benchmarks often report token- or reference-level accuracy rather than deployability or safety properties [4],[9]. We study a tightly constrained operational question grounded in preregistered design: How effective are template-based input sanitization plus deterministic verifier-gating (with at-most-one automated repair) at changing the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated CLI configurations when inputs are adversarially mutated? Our contributions are: (i) a preregistered confirmatory experiment (cand-2026-03) with a paired estimand measuring validator acceptance-for-deployment; (ii) artifact-backed quantitative results showing a small, statistically detectable absolute change in acceptance under a guarded pipeline vs an unguarded baseline on a synthetic adversarial intent bank; and (iii) explicit reviewer-requested reconciliations and artifact-grounded pipeline semantics (provider-call accounting, shared-initial semantics, and protocol-deviation disclosure). We emphasize that the preregistered natural-language hypothesis (that gating would reduce attacker-success) differs in interpretation from the registered formal estimand (paired validator acceptance difference); we report and interpret results strictly relative to the archived formal estimand.
sections.related_work: Deterministic verification tools (Header Space Analysis, NetPlumber, VeriFlow) provide formal checks of forwarding and configuration invariants and are natural validators for generate–validate pipelines [5]–[7]. Recent NetOps studies demonstrate that LLMs can produce useful configuration drafts but make syntax/semantic mistakes; integrating verifier feedback and repair improves prototype outcomes [3],[8]. Surveys of AIOps and telecommunications identify fragmented evaluation practices and call for operational metrics that reflect deployability and safety rather than token-level accuracy [4],[9]. Security research documents prompt-injection and indirect-prompt attacks against LLM-integrated systems, motivating input-sanitization and gating defenses [10]. Tool-augmented orchestration (Toolformer-style patterns) illustrates practical architectures where an LLM calls external checks and repairs based on feedback [11]. Our experiment is positioned as a preregistered, paired, artifact-backed test of sanitization+verifier-gating under a constrained synthetic adversary; it differs from prior work by preregistering a paired estimand and providing deterministic reconciliation of provider-call accounting.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand. The study cand-2026-03 was preregistered prior to observing outcomes (preregistration record included in the archive). The primary estimand is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline where each adversarial intent yields a binary outcome: 1 if the deterministic validator would accept the generated configuration for deployment, 0 otherwise. The confirmatory test is the exact two-sided McNemar on paired outcomes; precision was estimated by bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) as recorded in the archived analysis log. Design and task bank. The confirmatory paired design targeted N=150 adversarial intents (planned episodes = 300). Task templates (synthetic-netops intent templates) cover ACLs, interface admin changes, MTU and VLAN operations constrained to simple device groups; scope excludes any private production data. Model, validator, and orchestration. The archived run used the declared generator gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 under the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter (see execution/model_configuration.json and execution/execution_manifest.json in the archive). Shared-initial semantics and per-condition step listing. To address reviewer requests we explicitly list the per-condition sequence used in the archived run and point to artifact evidence supporting shared_initial_candidate reuse and provider-call accounting: 1) Orchestrator prepares the adversarially mutated intent (task manifest entry per pair_id). For the guarded variant the intent is also passed through a template-based input-sanitizer before generation; sanitization is designed to normalize or remove obviously adversarial constructs. 2) Shared initial generation: a single LLM generation call produces the shared_initial_candidate; the same initial candidate is used for the paired Baseline and Guarded evaluations (evidence: stage_counts.shared_initial_generation = 150 in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json and per-episode shared_initial_candidate paths such as execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt). 3) Baseline scoring: the deterministic validator checks the shared_initial_candidate and records acceptance/failure. 4) Guarded branch: the orchestrator applies verifier-gating; if the candidate fails the gating policy and per-preregs allowed policy, the orchestrator may invoke at-most-one permitted automated repair call to the LLM (repair stage). 5) Final validation: the validator re-checks repaired candidates; the final accepted/not-accepted decision determines the guarded outcome. Artifact evidence and provider-call accounting. Representative per-episode scoring artifacts show identical shared_initial_candidate content and the same shared_initial_candidate path for both conditions for a pair_id (examples: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json and execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json both reference execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt). The reconciled provider-call accounting archived at analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json documents hosted_model_call_event_count = 156, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 147, failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 9, and stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 150, repair = 6; these numbers confirm that extra model calls occurred only when repairs triggered. Missingness and exclusions. The preregistered missingness_plan excluded pairs only when both paired runs were technical failures. The archive records completed_episodes = 282, failed_episodes = 18, and complete_pairs_included = 141 (analysis/missingness_summary.csv). Protocol deviation: unset sampling temperature. The archived model configuration (execution/model_configuration.json) recorded an unset sampling temperature (temperature field null). We treat this as a protocol deviation from a fully specified sampling parameter because provider-side defaults may apply and could affect deterministic sampling. To preserve paired comparability despite potential provider-side sampling nondeterminism, the pipeline implemented shared_initial_candidate semantics (single shared generation per pair) and the reconciled provider-call accounting documents the exact call pattern used. Reproducibility note: reproductions desiring deterministic sampling should set temperature=0 explicitly when invoking the provider; the archive contains the exact run configuration and provider-call traces to enable reproduction under explicit provider semantics.
sections.results: Execution and basic counts. Planned episodes = 300; completed episodes = 282; failed episodes = 18; model_calls_used = 156 (execution/execution_manifest.json). Primary confirmatory analysis used the 141 complete pairs. Condition summary and paired contingency. Analysis/condition_summary.csv reports baseline_successes = 135/141 = 0.9574468085 and guarded_successes = 141/141 = 1.0. The paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is: n11 = 135; n10 (guarded=1, baseline=0) = 6; n01 = 0; n00 = 0. Statistical inference and interval estimation. Exact two-sided McNemar test on the paired outcomes yields p = 0.03125. The point estimate (guarded − baseline) is 0.04255319148936165. The 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) recorded in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl is [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]. Discordant-case diagnostics. The six discordant n10 pairs (guarded accepted while baseline failed) are documented in per-episode validator traces: in each documented case the guarded pipeline (via sanitization and/or the permitted repair call) altered candidate presentation or corrected a local ordering/format error such that deterministic_netops_validator_v5 marked the final configuration valid; the unguarded baseline candidate (same shared_initial_candidate) failed validation. The reconciliation stage_counts indicate repair=6, matching the number of discordant pairs and supporting the causal chain that permitted repairs produced the accepted guarded outcomes for those intents. Missingness sensitivity. Nine pairs were both-run failures and were excluded per the preregistered plan (analysis/missingness_summary.csv). A conservative sensitivity that treats both-missing pairs as failures yields baseline = 135/150 = 0.9000 and guarded = 141/150 = 0.9400; the discordant pair counts driving the primary exact test are unchanged and the McNemar p-value remains 0.03125 under this conservative mapping for interpretation. Unperformed preregistered items. The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and the false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed in the archived run; therefore we do not report empirical false-positive-blocking rates and caution that claims about blocking benign inputs cannot be made from this run.
sections.discussion: Interpretation relative to the formal estimand. Under the formal archival estimand (validator accepted-for-deployment), the guarded pipeline produced a small but statistically detectable absolute increase in validator-accepted candidates (≈4.255 percentage points) among included pairs. Because shared_initial_candidate semantics were used, the archive documents that paired differences arose from post-generation processing (sanitization and the at-most-one automated repair) and the validator gate rather than differing first-pass draws. Reconciliation with preregistered natural-language H1. The preregistered natural-language H1 asserted that verifier-gating would reduce attacker-success (fewer unsafe configurations accepted). The registered formal estimand measured acceptance-for-deployment (guarded − baseline) and is not equivalent to attacker-centric notions. In our data the guarded pipeline increased validator acceptance because sanitizer/repair enabled acceptance of reparable candidates that the baseline failed; this outcome does not prove decreased attacker-success under an attacker-centric definition (e.g., acceptance of malicious or safety-violating payloads under a broader semantic-safety oracle). We therefore avoid equating the archived formal result with an attacker-centric success reduction. Operational implications. In this constrained synthetic setting: (i) template-based sanitization plus limited automated repair can recover valid, deployable configurations that an unguarded baseline fails to produce; (ii) deterministic gating functions as a safety boundary but its operational effect depends on whether the system permits repair operations that modify otherwise rejected drafts; co-design between gating and repair policies is required to avoid rejecting reparable generations or, conversely, accepting repaired but semantically unsafe outputs if repair logic is inadequate. Threats to validity. Internal validity: 18 technical failures reduced effective N; paired exclusion (both-run failures = 9) was preregistered and applied. Protocol deviation: an unset runtime temperature was recorded in execution/model_configuration.json; provider-side defaults could affect sampling determinism but shared_initial semantics preserved paired comparability for this run. Construct validity: the deterministic validator encodes a limited set of safety properties (CLI grammar, required sequences, protected-interface invariants) and omits some protocol-level dynamic runtime semantics; acceptance-for-deployment is therefore only a partial proxy for operational safety. External validity: single-generator (gpt-5-mini), single-validator, synthetic intents and narrow device semantics limit generalization to multi-vendor, production networks. Conclusion validity: the observed absolute effect is small and occurs against a high baseline acceptance rate (ceiling effect). The statistical result (p = 0.03125; 95% CI excludes zero) supports a detectable difference in this experimental setup but does not imply large practical gains broadly. Recommendations for future work. Execute the preregistered benign-control and measure false-positive blocking; define and measure an explicit attacker-centric estimand (e.g., acceptance of unsafe configurations under a comprehensive semantic-safety oracle); diversify generators and validators across vendors and protocols; and fix sampling settings (temperature=0) for deterministic reproduction when desired. All above recommendations follow directly from limitations observed in the archived run and the recorded artifacts.
sections.conclusion: A preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment on a synthetic adversarial intent bank found that template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating and at-most-one automated repair produced a small but statistically detectable increase in deterministic-validator-accepted LLM-generated configurations under the archived formal estimand (paired difference ≈ 0.04255; p = 0.03125; 95% CI [0.01418, 0.07801]). Diagnostic artifacts (per-episode validator traces and reconciliation stage_counts) indicate the six discordant pairs were associated with permitted repair calls. Importantly, this improvement does not equate to measured reduction in attacker-success under an attacker-centric definition and is limited by synthetic scope, single-model/validator evaluation, and a protocol deviation in runtime sampling. Future work should execute the preregistered benign-control, explicitly measure attacker-centric estimands, diversify models and validators, and fix sampling parameters for reproducible deterministic runs. All numeric and accounting statements above are supported by archived execution and analysis artifacts referenced in Methods and Results (see artifact paths listed in the Disclosure Statement).

Declared models/tools and orchestration: primary generator = gpt-5-mini (see execution/model_configuration.json in the archive), deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5, task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5, orchestration adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Runtime sampling settings: the archived model configuration recorded an unset sampling temperature (temperature field null in execution/model_configuration.json); this is reported as a protocol deviation because provider-side defaults may affect sampling determinism and we discuss its implications in Methods and Discussion. Provider-call accounting and execution accounting referenced in the manuscript are archived and include analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json, execution/execution_manifest.json, execution/raw_results.jsonl, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, and analysis/condition_summary.csv. Shared_initial_candidate semantics and per-episode traces demonstrating reuse across paired conditions are archived (examples: execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt and execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json and execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json). Missingness and failure accounting are archived (analysis/missingness_summary.csv). No human manually edited or corrected the manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock. Full run traces, tool-call logs, validator traces, and archived analysis artifacts referenced above are included in the submitted evidence bundle for verification.
limitations: Synthetic task bank and intent templates — not real production traffic or operator logs; results may not generalize to field datasets.
Single-model evaluation (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation limit external validity across vendors, protocols, and model families.
Validator coverage constrained to encoded safety properties (CLI grammar, required sequences, protected-interface invariants); some protocol-level or dynamic runtime semantics are not represented.
Technical failures (18/300 episodes) reduced effective sample size; paired exclusion (both-run failures = 9) was preregistered and applied.
Adversary model limited to mutations of synthetic intents; prompt-injection in retrieval-augmented or multi-source pipelines was not exhaustively evaluated here.
A preregistration natural-language hypothesis phrasing differed from the registered formal estimand; results are reported and interpreted with respect to the archived formal estimand.
The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed; therefore no empirical false-positive-blocking claims are made.
